Adds a Delay Gate block. On the first reach, it starts a one-time timer and skips its contained actions. The surrounding script continues immediately.

This block does not schedule an execution. Its timer is checked only when the script reaches the same block instance again. Reaches before the timer expires skip the contained actions. The first reach at or after expiry opens the gate and runs them; every later reach runs them immediately.

Delay time is in milliseconds. A resolved delay of 0 or less, including invalid values, opens the gate immediately.

The gate resets only when that action-script instance is reconstructed or replaced.

Use Execute Later instead when every reach should schedule a fresh delayed execution.

Adds an Execute Later block that schedules its contained actions to run after the specified delay.

Delay time is in milliseconds.

Every time the script reaches this block, it schedules a new execution on the main thread.

This is useful for delayed actions in scripts that only run once.
